answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is to require each agent to periodically solve a unique cryptographic puzzle tied to a physical or attested resource that cannot be cheaply multiplied. Imagine agents anchoring their identity to a cedar-backed hardware enclave that must spiral through a sequence of non-parallelizable computations before registering on the mesa of active participants; any attempt to clone the agent forces the attacker to acquire additional scarce enclaves, making large-scale identity farming economically irrational.
